name: binary-search-tree
description: Implement a binary search tree with insert, search, and traversal methods

promptLevels.beginner: create a binary search tree class
promptLevels.intermediate: implement a binary search tree with insert and search operations
promptLevels.advanced: create a BinarySearchTree class with insert, search, and inorder traversal methods that work with numbers
promptLevels.expert: Implement a `BinarySearchTree` class with the following methods: `insert(value: number): void` to add a value, `search(value: number): boolean` to check if a value exists, and `inorderTraversal(): number[]` to return values in sorted order. {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use TypeScript with proper type annotations for the TreeNode and BinarySearchTree classes. Export only the BinarySearchTree class.
languageInstructions.javascript: Use JavaScript with a TreeNode class for nodes. Export only the BinarySearchTree class.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use JavaScript with JSDoc annotations for all methods and classes. Include @param and @return tags. Export only the BinarySearchTree class.

variants.typescript: Implement a `BinarySearchTree` class in TypeScript with proper type annotations. Include: `insert(value: number): void`, `search(value: number): boolean`, and `inorderTraversal(): number[]`. Use a private TreeNode class or interface. Export only the BinarySearchTree class.
variants.javascript: Implement a `BinarySearchTree` class in JavaScript. Include: `insert(value)`, `search(value)`, and `inorderTraversal()`. Use a TreeNode class for nodes. Export only the BinarySearchTree class.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Implement a `BinarySearchTree` class in JavaScript with full JSDoc annotations. Include @param and @return tags for: `insert(value)`, `search(value)`, and `inorderTraversal()`. Export only the BinarySearchTree class.

testCases.test: const bst = new BinarySearchTree(); bst.insert(5); console.assert(bst.search(5) === true, 'Should find inserted value');
const bst = new BinarySearchTree(); bst.insert(5); console.assert(bst.search(10) === false, 'Should not find non-existent value');

const bst = new BinarySearchTree(); [5,3,7,1,4,6,8].forEach(v => bst.insert(v)); const result = bst.inorderTraversal(); console.assert(JSON.stringify(result) === '[1,3,4,5,6,7,8]', 'Inorder traversal should return sorted array');
const bst = new BinarySearchTree(); bst.insert(10); bst.insert(5); bst.insert(15); console.assert(bst.search(5) === true && bst.search(15) === true, 'Should find all inserted values');
const bst = new BinarySearchTree(); const result = bst.inorderTraversal(); console.assert(Array.isArray(result) && result.length === 0, 'Empty tree should return empty array');
